summary: Wiesbaden's municipal company WiBau runs five city garages (about 1,870 spaces) under the Lilienparken brand presented in December 2025, while Contipark operates the RMCC and Kurhaus/Casino garages and Q-Park the Lili garage. From the start of 2025 WiBau's downtown garages moved to 15- or 20-minute billing steps (shortest stay EUR 0.50) and the Luisenplatz hourly rate was cut from EUR 3 to EUR 2; by May 2026, 479 of the Lilienparken spaces had charging points. Resident parking costs EUR 120 a year, an environmental zone has existed since 2013, a February 2019 settlement with Deutsche Umwelthilfe averted a diesel ban, and the Citybahn tram was rejected by 62.1% in a November 2020 referendum. A CDU-FDP-Greens-Volt coalition treaty presented in August 2026, subject to party approval, envisages a trial switch-off of the Berliner Straße Pförtnerampel.

items.text: The city's page on air quality states that an environmental zone (Umweltzone) was introduced in 2013 because of high pollutant values; NO2 at the Schiersteiner Straße and Ringkirche stations has roughly halved since 2015, with a particularly sharp decline in 2019.
items.source_title: Lufthygiene (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden)

items.text: Wiesbaden avoided a diesel driving ban: Deutsche Umwelthilfe (DUH) and VCD, who had sued the state of Hesse, settled their case at the administrative court on 13 February 2019 after the city presented its updated clean air plan (NO2 reached up to 48 µg/m3 in 2018 against a 40 limit). During the hearing the city announced it wanted to retrofit not only 100 diesel buses but also refuse collection vehicles, and said it planned to expand the cycling network, introduce electric buses and create new park-and-ride spaces, aiming to meet the limit by 2020.
items.source_title: Kein Diesel-Fahrverbot in Wiesbaden (zfk)

items.text: In the binding referendum of 1 November 2020 62.1% of voters rejected the Citybahn tram (about 40 km, Mainz-Wiesbaden-Bad Schwalbach, estimated cost EUR 426 million); turnout was 46.2% and the 31,500-vote quorum was met. Mayor Gert-Uwe Mende said the result must be respected but the traffic status quo cannot remain.
items.source_title: Wiesbaden: Klares Nein zur City-Bahn (zfk)

items.text: The city's resident parking page states a Bewohnerparken permit costs EUR 120 per year (EUR 10 per month); the regime applies Monday to Friday 9:00-22:00, visitors can park free for up to one hour in most zones (two hours in some).
items.source_title: Bewohnerparken: Entspannt parken, komfortabel leben (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden)

items.text: Hessenschau reported that Deutsche Umwelthilfe considers Wiesbaden's EUR 120 resident-parking permit too cheap and wants a minimum of EUR 360 per year.
items.source_title: Deutsche Umwelthilfe findet Anwohnerparken zu billig (hessenschau)

items.text: Hessenschau reported (7 Oct 2025) that, according to the city, Wiesbaden had no plans to extend its parking zone or raise parking or resident-permit fees (EUR 120 a year, EUR 70 for six months); about EUR 1.16 million net was raised from permits in 2024 and is used entirely to fund a discounted pupils' ticket (Schülerticket) at EUR 10 or 15 per month.
items.source_title: Hier wird das Parken in Hessen teurer - Städte passen Gebühren an (hessenschau)

items.text: WiBau GmbH restructured tariffs in the city-owned garages from 1 January 2025: the downtown garages (Luisenplatz, Theater, City II, Mauritiusgalerie), previously billed hourly, moved to 15- or 20-minute billing steps so the shortest stay costs 50 cents; at Luisenplatz the hourly rate fell from EUR 3 to EUR 2.
items.source_title: Neue Parktarife für Wiesbadens Parkhäuser (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release, 14 Feb 2025)

items.text: The same press release states WiBau currently operates five garages and underground garages plus car parks with about 1,900 spaces in total, and says all facilities are to be converted to automatic licence plate recognition, cashless payment is to be improved (for example monthly account debit for registered customers) and, after modernisation, free spaces can be shown on parken-in-wiesbaden.de.
items.source_title: Neue Parktarife für Wiesbadens Parkhäuser (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release, 14 Feb 2025)

items.text: From April 2025 WiBau introduced a new tariff at the Warmer Damm car park by Wilhelmstraße: the first 20 minutes are free and each further 10 minutes costs EUR 1, aimed at short-stay turnover; the Theater garage is named as the cheaper option for longer stays.
items.source_title: Neues Parkkonzept am Warmen Damm: Kostenlose Kurzzeit-Parkplätze in Wiesbaden (Wiesbadenaktuell)

items.text: For the 2025 Advent weekends (Friday-Sunday) all municipal garages offered a EUR 5 per day flat rate, with listed capacities: Mauritiusgalerie 432, City II 415, Theater 302, Luisenplatz 292, plus Friedrich-Ebert-Allee 185 (EUR 5 daily year-round); the RMCC underground garage charged EUR 6 per day. Public transport was free on the four Advent Saturdays.
items.source_title: Parken an Adventswochenenden (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release, 2 Dec 2025)

items.text: On 18 December 2025 WiBau, the municipal parking company, presented 'Lilienparken' as a new umbrella brand for the city-run parking facilities it manages (CEO Andreas Guntrum; Traffic Councillor Andreas Kowol), saying the brand stands for reliability, fairness, quality and modern service; the release adds that the tariff structure introduced at the start of 2025 was meant to counter Wiesbaden's image as an 'expensive parking city'.
items.source_title: Neue Dachmarke für städtische Parkhäuser (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release)

items.text: A WiBau press release of 18 December 2025 said all its parking facilities now had digital licence plate recognition and announced that, from January 2026, short-term parkers without a rental contract could register to skip the pay machine, with monthly direct-debit billing and 10% off all parking, and that from February 2026 monthly rental contracts would be handled through a new digital registration tool.
items.source_title: Neue Dachmarke für städtische Parkhäuser (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release)

items.text: The city's long-term and night parking page lists monthly tariffs at Parkhaus Mauritiusgalerie and Parkhaus City of EUR 160 for all-day (24/7) and EUR 60 for a night tariff (Mon-Fri 17:00-09:00, weekends and holidays all day); Parkhaus Elsässer Platz (WiBau, open since July 2024) has 429 spaces.
items.source_title: Dauer- und Nachtparken (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden)

items.text: The city's RMCC visitor page states the garage beneath the RheinMain CongressCenter has 800 spaces, open 24 hours, operated by Contipark Parkgaragengesellschaft mbH; tariff EUR 2.50 per hour (maximum EUR 12 per day), 8 spaces with EV charging, dynamic signage showing free spaces.
items.source_title: Parking | RheinMain CongressCenter Wiesbaden

items.text: The same page lists nearby alternatives: Parkhaus Luisenplatz (320 spaces, 5-minute walk) and Q-Park Lili/Liliencarree (1,101 spaces, 10-minute walk); it also names the Kurhaus underground garage (520 spaces, Contipark, about 12 minutes).
items.source_title: Parking | RheinMain CongressCenter Wiesbaden

items.text: The city's Kurhaus access page says the garage beneath the bowling green is operated by Contipark and has 450 spaces plus 70 outdoor spaces; the Theater garage (stated as 320 spaces) is a one-minute walk away.
items.source_title: Arrival | Kurhaus Wiesbaden

items.text: The same page says the city centre has eleven parking garages with 5,106 spaces plus 1,490 spaces in five large car parks, and that parking guidance boards at the entrance roads show the direction to the nearest garage and the current number of free spaces.
items.source_title: Arrival | Kurhaus Wiesbaden

items.text: Q-Park operates the Lili garage under the Lili shopping centre at Bahnhofplatz 3 (about 1 minute from the main station): EUR 1 per hour, daytime (06-22) maximum EUR 6.50, night (22-06) maximum EUR 3.50, daily maximum EUR 10.
items.source_title: Parking at the Lili in Wiesbaden (Q-Park)

items.text: The city's Park & Ride page lists P&R sites at Moltkering (~218 spaces), Kahle Mühle (~250), Mainzer Straße Ost (~120) and West (~50), Stadion Berliner Straße (~100) and Kleinaustraße (~70), all free, with one exception, Salzbachaue, which is charged.
items.source_title: Park & Ride in Wiesbaden (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden)

items.text: A 16-point fast-charging park (Deutschlandnetz, up to 400 kW per point) is being built on the Salzbachaue car park at Gartenfeldstraße near the main station; partial closures began 26 May 2026, wider closures were expected from 15 June and completion was targeted for early September 2026.
items.source_title: Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden unterstützt Ausbau der Elektromobilität: Neuer Schnellladepark am Hauptbahnhof (press release, 28 May 2026)

items.text: WiBau runs five Lilienparken garages with 1,870 spaces, of which 479 spaces now have charging points; 20 more charging points (16 AC, 4 DC) went into operation at Parkhaus Luisenplatz in March-April 2026, and Parkhaus Elsässer Platz has 429 charging points including 8 DC fast chargers, with 45 minutes of free parking while charging.
items.source_title: Lilienparken baut Ladenetz in Parkhäusern weiter aus (Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden press release, 29 May 2026)

items.text: Hessenschau reported on 13 Aug 2026 that CDU, FDP, Greens and Volt agreed a coalition treaty with a one-vote majority; it envisages reviewing a return to 50 km/h on arterial roads and testing a temporary shutdown of the Berliner Straße Pförtnerampel (traffic-metering light introduced for air quality), with ratification due in the following weeks.
items.source_title: Koalitionsvertrag steht: Maracuja-Koalition will Wiesbaden neu aufstellen (hessenschau)
